status: POST-HOC DEV RESEARCH — temporal-GP development; not confirmatory; C3 reserved

data.population: NEW, 135 runs with an aligned bounds/time record (H-e7dbd8e5ce has none: a paid query without a trajectory, absent from test scoring)
data.checkpoints: repeats 1-2 x folds 1-5 x budgets 16/40/80 = 30; training = Week 19 pilot shared label-blind paid prefixes (tables/paid_paths.csv); complete runs held out
data.target: y = log(1 + depth_um) on s = t / derived_exit; depth = 0 on rows without melt; native monitor time from iter.dat -> time.dat
data.planned_horizon: s_plan = min(TE, 0.9 exit) / exit (pre-query scheduled settings)
data.observed_window: s_obs = min(recording end, 0.9 exit) / exit (scoring support only; no stretching or tail filling)
data.compression: per-bin means on a uniform s-grid of K bins over [0, 0.9]; each training run also contributes its exact native maximum (s, y) to the separable GP
data.resolution_rule: For each checkpoint, K is the smallest value in (90, 180, 360, 720) whose median, over the PAID training runs, of the RMSE between the native log1p-depth series and its bin-mean reconstruction (observed window only) is <= 0.04; if none qualifies, K = 720 and the checkpoint is flagged.  Test runs never influence K.

models.scalar_A_GP: Week 19 ACTIVE E1 regression (src.week18_engine DepthGPR on log A, ML-II, one start), refitted on the same paid prefixes; must equal the pilot's saved predictions
models.mean_trajectory: input-free training mean per bin (no fit)
models.functional_rank3: per-bin training mean + rank-3 basis from alternating least squares on observed training entries only (no imputation as data); three coefficient GPs (sklearn, ConstantKernel x Matern-3/2 ARD + white noise, ML-II, one start) on training-standardized log inputs; global residual variance

separable_SVGP.inducing_init: fixed-seed random subset of the training inputs; locations learned
separable_SVGP.optimizer: Adam on all hyperparameters, variational and inducing parameters
separable_SVGP.why_not_kronecker: training design is a staircase (each run covers [0, s_obs]); Kronecker identities need a complete grid with common noise; validated on a complete synthetic grid only

uncertainty: maximum, argmax timing and exceedance distributions from 2000 posterior latent trajectories per held-out run (never the maximum of the posterior mean); scalar A from its predictive lognormal
evaluation: simulation-weighted trajectory RMSE (observed bins) and median
50 %/90 % pointwise interval coverage and width (latent + noise variance)
A error (um, log1p) vs native maximum and vs bin-mean maximum; 90 % interval coverage of A
argmax timing error (us) and time-above-u_ref error (us) on the observed window
short-event analysis: near-peak (>= 95 % of A) episode shorter than one bin
runtime, peak memory, SVGP ELBO trace, SVGP vs exact on a controlled example, M=400 vs M=800 at one checkpoint
representative best / median / worst held-out runs and the named runs (matched pair, late negative)
planned-horizon vs observed-window quantities reported separately for the six truncated runs

hypotheses.T2-H1_inputs_help: At every budget (B16/B40/B80) both temporal models (rank-3 functional and separable SVGP) have lower simulation-weighted trajectory RMSE (log1p depth, observed bins) than the input-free training-mean trajectory. Basis: depth trajectories depend strongly on scan speed (slow scans near 300 um, fast scans near 110 um). Falsified if either model is not lower at any budget.
hypotheses.T2-H2_learning: Trajectory RMSE of both temporal models decreases from B16 to B80 (mean over the ten folds). Falsified otherwise.
hypotheses.T2-H3_max_depth: For the maximum depth A of held-out runs (like-for-like runs, observed window = planned horizon), the scalar A GP has a lower median absolute error (um) than both temporal models at B40 and at B80. Basis: the scalar model targets A directly, while bin means lose 0.004-0.02 log1p units at the native peak (measured compression gap). Falsified if a temporal model is lower at B40 or B80.
hypotheses.T2-H4_short_events: The temporal models' underestimation of A (relative to the native maximum) is larger for runs whose near-peak episode (depth >= 95 % of A) is shorter than one bin width than for longer episodes. Basis: bin means smooth sub-bin peaks by construction.
hypotheses.T2-H5_calibration: No numerical expectation. 50 % and 90 % pointwise predictive intervals are evaluated on observed bins, together with interval coverage for A.
hypotheses.T2-H6_model_ranking: No directional expectation between the functional baseline and the separable SVGP.
hypotheses.T2-H7_matched_pair_fast_scans: No assumption either way. Evaluated: (a) whether the observed trajectories of the matched pair (H-b302fc6cbd vs H-b7e3ed2e12) differ beyond each model's predictive uncertainty; (b) whether the models' predictions for the two runs differ; (c) descriptively, whether trajectory features (predicted A, predicted time above u_ref) rank held-out labels within fast scans (VX > 0.85; exploratory). Trajectory accuracy and canonical-label information are reported separately; no classifier is built.
hypotheses.T2-H8_truncated: For the six runs whose recording ends before the planned horizon, planned-horizon predicted maxima and observed-window maxima are reported separately as different estimands. No expectation.
